text: Good afternoon, everybody.

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So today we're going to talk about how do we enable anyone at your company to ship.

text: There are lots of people at your company that have great ideas of things that will solve problems inside your company.

text: But even with AI, the technology still holds them back.

text: It's pretty easy now.

text: But shipping it, making it available, even internally to your company, hasn't really gotten that much easier, right?

text: And so, you know, for a less technical person, for a non-engineer, they're going to struggle with, you know, do I put it on Vercel?

text: They might not know the details of how to do that.

text: Even for engineers who know how these tools work, they don't really want to have to go through this and do it from scratch every single time.

text: And then if you're deploying these things internally, you want them to have auth and security baked in.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You don't want people just shipping API keys to stuff that might get checked into code bases or stuff like that.

text: And so what do you do?

text: You end up burning a bunch of engineering time to say, hey, this is important.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We need to go convert this to be some proper app deployment.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the thing we needed at WorkOS was kind of two things.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: One, the capability for everyone at the company to build and ship an application.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They shouldn't need to go ask infra for provisioning.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They shouldn't need to get security approval for standard apps.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They should just be able to build the thing and make it available.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And two, we want a distribution.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: As soon as they ship it, they can link someone else to it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: That person can click the link in Slack, open it up, and access the application without any red flags or any kind of red tape.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We wanted to move fast.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We wanted to build quickly.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We have this applied AI team at WorkOS whose their singular job is, how do we make AI more and more useful across the company?

text: We need to get the feedback around it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Turns out we basically had sort of a forcing function to gather feedback, which is we started doing these company-wide Claude days.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Basically, it's a single-day hackathon where everyone pairs up into teams and builds an app.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And typically, when we do this, we actually pair non-engineers with engineers.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we actually have the non-engineers do the building.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They're the ones that have our hands on keyboard.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They're the ones building the application, while the engineer that's paired with them is there to consult, help them, unblock them with any issues they find so they don't get stuck, kind of be a sounding board for how they can approach this.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But we have a ton of our marketing folks and sales folks that have all these really great ideas of apps that they've maybe struggled to bring to life.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we built two things.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The first thing is we built a CLI.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We call it WOW.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: WOW is the thing that helps you build and generate an app without needing to know any of the underlying details.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It basically is a toolkit that helps you set up Git, set up a repo, clone in an example application that you can use to start with for Claude Code or Codex to build the app you want to build.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we distribute it to every single employee at the company through our MDM.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We just push it on your machine so every employee, day one, has access to this tool.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The WoW CLI lets you run things like WoW App Create.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: What it does is that you name the app, it scans your machine and says, okay, do you have Git installed?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Are you logged into GitHub?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Do you have Doppler, which is where you do secrets management?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It kind of does all this pre-configuration of your developer machine, whether you're an engineer or not, so that everything is kind of ready to go and you're not going to hit any snags along the way.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We also built a shared skills repository.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So anyone at the company can, if they've built a skill that's useful, they can push that skill up, and it's shared to everyone, and then it's easy to fetch those skills, see what's available, and pull skills down to help you build things or do certain workflows.

text: So I want to talk a little bit about Atlas, which is the actual platform underneath this that empowers this tool.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: WoW is just sort of the CLI that people use to interface with it, but Atlas is actually the underlying infrastructure.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Basically, Atlas allows you to create, build, deploy, and share these applications.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The sort of three principles when we were building Atlas that we wanted to maintain and ensure that provided a great experience.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: One was we wanted the infrared to be invisible.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: No one should need to know where the deployment target is.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It happens to be that we're running on Cloudflare workers.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: If at some point we want to change that to Vercel or AWS, it shouldn't matter.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It should be transparent to anyone trying to build and deploy these applications.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We want to be secured by default.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We don't want to risk those.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: I can't show you all of the apps that we built.

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we don't want anyone to just be able to access these tools outside the company because they're very sensitive.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then last is the discoverability.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Someone shares a link in Slack.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Anyone should be able to click that and be able to view that tool.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So today Atlas runs on Cloudflare's developer platform.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It's already part of the package.

text: And we automatically host all of these tools when you push them under workos.tools.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we have this shared domain that whatever your app is called, you get that host name underneath workos.tools.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So you don't have to worry about where is the app going to be available, how does it get, you know, do people get access.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00
